evals.prompt: у меня сервис app/main.py крутится под systemd, вчера папка logs/ выросла до 12 гигов и диск забился. сделай чтобы логи никогда не занимали больше 500 МБ, и чтоб это было проверено тестом
evals.expected_output: Time-only rotation is replaced by size-based rotation whose maxBytes x (backupCount+1) fits the 500 MB budget, plus a start-up prune that trims the logs folder by total size; the per-second DEBUG dump of the whole payload is removed or shortened; a test proves the cap with large (sparse) files; journald is mentioned as a separate, manual limit.
assertions: The service's log file handler rotates by size (RotatingFileHandler or equivalent) and its maxBytes x (backupCount + 1) is at most 500 MB
There is code that trims the logs folder by total size (deleting the oldest files until under the budget), not only by age
A test creates files whose total exceeds the budget and asserts the folder ends up at or under it, and the run shows the test passing
The full payload is no longer logged at DEBUG every second (the line is removed, shortened, or replaced by a count)
The final answer mentions journald / systemd journal size as a separate limit and does not edit files under /etc

evals.prompt: в worker/jobs.py логи бесполезные: строки от разных задач вперемешку, "job failed: timeout" а какая задача и сколько шла - непонятно. переделай логирование так чтобы по id задачи сразу было видно всё что с ней случилось
evals.expected_output: Each job produces exactly one structured (JSON) event written at the end of the job, carrying the job id, outcome ok/error with the error type/message, duration and the steps' facts (fetch size, summary length); scattered per-step lines and the page-body dump are gone; a failing job is recorded and the loop continues; running the worker shows one event per job.
assertions: Running the worker produces exactly one JSON log line per job (3 jobs -> 3 event lines)
Each job event contains the job id, a duration in ms, and an outcome field; the failing job's event has outcome error with the error type (ConnectionError) and message
The page body is not written to the log (only its length or nothing), and the per-step info lines of the original are removed or folded into the event
After job 2 fails, job 3 still runs and gets its own event
